<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/field.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/field.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `35ead69fa30f2f8f9ffb12339bb9cd83de1f4bc0` — the merge of head `d8b82f70d50a48747586e5281279e091ce9c9331` into base `441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 35ead69fa30f2f8f9ffb12339bb9cd83de1f4bc0 && git checkout 35ead69fa30f2f8f9ffb12339bb9cd83de1f4bc0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590 d8b82f70d50a48747586e5281279e091ce9c9331 && git checkout -B drift-repro 441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590 && git merge --no-ff d8b82f70d50a48747586e5281279e091ce9c9331

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `197434e99892c47512a9c91e84e243fa8fcc97e0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/field.json, packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-show-on-create.test.ts

PR #36449, card #36425, PR 1 of 2. Read: the card body and its five comments, the PR body and its one comment, the ten-file net diff against `main` (merge base `ff60149900`), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read in the head tree only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, the one change.** `FieldSchema` is a `strictObject` (field.zod.ts:1647). Before this head it refused the key `showOnCreate` as an unrecognized key. It now accepts `showOnCreate: true` and `showOnCreate: false` on any field. Right, and a pure widening.
- **The refused pair is inside the new space.** `showOnCreate: false` beside `required: true` is refused by the new `superRefine` block (field.zod.ts:3232), at path `showOnCreate`, code `custom`. Every input that pair names was already refused on `main`, as an unknown key. Nothing that parsed before is refused now. Right.
- **Nothing is reshaped.** The key is `z.boolean().optional()` with no default. The `.overwrite()` step does not touch it. A field that does not author the key parses to the same output, key for key. The test pins the absence (`'showOnCreate' in data` is false). Right.
- **Where the key is reachable.** `ObjectSchema.fields` and the migration `field` slot take `FieldSchema` whole, so both gain the key. The three regenerated reference pages agree. `ObjectExtensionSchema.fieldPatches` is built from `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST` (label, description, inlineHelpText, placeholder), so an extension can patch neither `showOnCreate` nor `required`. The refusal cannot be bypassed through a patch. Right.
- **Public surface.** One new optional key on the inferred field type and one row in `authorable-surface/data.json` (`data/Field:showOnCreate`). Additive. Right.
- **Liveness.** `liveness/field.json` grades the key `planned`, with the parse refusal as evidence, and the count file moves from 5 to 6 planned. No reader of the key exists anywhere in the head tree (a full grep finds the schema, the test, the ledger and generated pages only). `planned` is the honest grade. Right.
- **Form reconciliation.** The `omit` row for `field.showOnCreate` follows the five existing `planned, not yet rendered` rows in the same ledger. Not offering a switch that nothing honours is the ADR-0078 reading. Right.
- **Check-runs.** Green at review time: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Lint docs and code guards, Lint repo and tooling gates, Lint CI release and engine gates, Lint ESLint, Lint PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped lint runs, Type Check source gates, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Regression Gate. **Pending, not judged:** Test Core 1 to 10, Test UI 1 to 16, Build Core, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Type Check UI, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates, Type Check debt ledger. This record does not vouch for a pending run.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset is `@objectstack/spec` minor. An `added` kind on the published spec takes at least minor. Minor is right, and Check Changeset is green.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right for this diff. The only accept-set move is the new key, and the refused pair was never accepted.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` is right. One authorable key is added, none is removed, renamed or re-meant.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` is acceptable. No skill should teach a key that has no reader yet. The debt is real and is PR 2's.
- `Part of #36425` is right. The card's acceptance lines are all UI readings and none is met by this PR.
- The card's claim still reads `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. Those describe the whole card. They do not describe this diff, and the claim should be amended when PR 2 opens, as the PR body says.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in the os-dev-report (7079007194) is empty. Nothing to answer.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: no review request was sent, because the relay has no such op. That is the seat's carrier matter, not a contract point.
- `security_findings: withheld` in the report. No detail is on the card, so it cannot be judged here. The seat should confirm with the dev whether a finding exists. This review found no security-sensitive mechanism in the diff.
- **Rulings cited but not on the card.** The PR body and report cite "the seat's rulings" for three things: `defaultValue` is no exception, `requiredWhen` is accepted, and the lint notice, Studio switch and skills text move to PR 2. No card comment records them. They were judged here from the tree alone. The move of the lint notice and the Studio switch to PR 2 is sound on its own terms: the notice would say a form is no longer loaded while it still is, and a switch offered before a reader exists is what ADR-0078 rules out. The `defaultValue` arm is S1 below. The seat should record these rulings on the card.
- **ADR-0085 §2.** The jsdoc cites the admission test. §2 is written for `ObjectSchema` presentation keys, and the ADR carries no note for this key at this head. The reading itself holds: which fields a business asks for at creation is not inferable, and the name names a lifecycle moment, not a page. The maintainer approved the switch on the card. The ADR note is owed on #36086.
- **SQL push-down.** The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no join. Nothing to flag.
- **Dogfood battery.** `n/a` is right: no narrowing arm and no rendered surface.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts**

- The key, its type and its absence semantics hold against the card (item 5: a switch, default on) and against the first consumer PR 2 names. Absent reads as on, so no stored field changes meaning.
- The refusal sits in the field's own `superRefine`, so every door that parses a field reaches it. The object door locates it at `fields.NAME.showOnCreate`, and the test pins that path.
- `requiredWhen` is accepted. That holds: the parse cannot judge a predicate, and the describe says the create is still refused when the predicate holds and the value is empty.
- The refusal is stricter than its siblings. `hidden: true` or `readonly: true` beside `required: true` carry the same hazard and parse today. That is a deliberate choice for a new key, not a defect.

S1 (should-fix) — The stated reason for refusing the pair when a `defaultValue` is declared does not hold against the write door. The comment at field.zod.ts:3225 says that together "no record of the object could be created from the platform's create surfaces", and the message says a default is "not a guarantee that the create carries one". But `insert()` resolves `defaultValue`s before it validates, "so a required field carrying a default is never missing by the time `validateRecord` runs" (packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts:139, measured there on `tier: { required: true, defaultValue: 'standard' }`; record-validator.ts:2390 says the same). A create surface that leaves the field out sends no key, so a static default always fills it and the create passes. The card's own reason for item 6 ("否则新建永远过不了") is therefore untrue for a defaulted field. This is also the most common hide-on-create case (a required `status` with a default), and the message steers its author to drop `required`, which weakens the write contract. Two honest fixes, either one closes this: (a) admit the pair when the field declares a `defaultValue`, which is still a pure widening, with a control case in the test; or (b) keep the refusal as the conservative choice, record the ruling on the card, and rewrite the comment, the message, the describe clause and the changeset sentence so they state the real reason (for example: a default can evaluate empty, and the platform refuses the pair until that is ruled). Refusing now and widening later is semver-safe, so (b) does not block the release. What cannot stand is a published refusal message whose reason the engine contradicts.

- Nit: the describe is in the present tense ("`false`: no create surface shows it") while no reader exists. The changeset says so plainly and the ledger says `planned`, which matches the house pattern (`conditionalFormatting`, `referenceDeletedWhen`). No change asked.
- Nit: `required: true` with the field's own `visibleWhen` is "required when shown", so that triple can also create successfully. It falls under the same choice as S1.

**packages/spec/liveness/field.json** (implementing)

- The row agrees with the tree: `planned`, evidence is the parse refusal, the note names the readers and the flip. It carries no `authorWarn`, like the other planned field rows. See the standalone point below.

**packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts** (implementing)

- The omit row agrees with the ledger grade and names its own deletion in PR 2. Holds.

**packages/spec/src/data/field-show-on-create.test.ts** (implementing)

- The three refusal cases assert the located issue: count one, path ending `showOnCreate`, code `custom`, the message's first sentence, and the object-door path. The reported ablation (condition set to `false`, 3 of 3 red, controls green) fits what these cases read. They do pin the new refusal.
- The acceptance side is pinned by full `safeParse` success on four controls and by the parsed value for `true` and `false`. That pins the widening itself.
- Nit: the second case is titled "naming both remedies" but matches only the first sentence. If S1 takes route (a), the `defaultValue` case flips to a control. If it takes route (b), that case should pin the corrected sentence.

**Does PR 1 stand alone if PR 2 never lands?**

- Yes, with one caveat. Nothing existing breaks, nothing is reshaped, and the revert is one commit. The key would then be parsed and unread: an author who writes `showOnCreate: false` gets no warning, and the reference page states a behaviour nothing implements. The ledger row is honest about it, and the form does not offer it. If PR 2 slips past the next release cut, the row should take `authorWarn: true` or the describe a not-yet-enforced marker. That is a follow-up condition, not a finding on this head.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b86db2be460ae3c2d4393353c71117324c549f6d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/field.json, packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-show-on-create.test.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/builtin-column-collision.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts

Delta review of PR #36449 (card #36425, PR 1 of 2). The previous record is PASS 7079100809 at `197434e9`. Read this round: the card body and its six comments (the seat's rulings 7079131071 included), the PR body and its two comments, the range `197434e9..b86db2be` in full, the thirteen-file net file list, and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read on `main` at `ff60149900`, which is still the merge base.

**The range.** Four commits, each with one parent: `2eaa2bc9`, `1c0012aa`, `e89912af`, `b86db2be`. There is no merge of `main` in it, so every hunk is the PR's own. Nine files move: `field.zod.ts`, its test, the changeset, three regenerated reference pages, and the three pin files. `liveness/field.json`, `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts`, `authorable-surface/data.json` and `liveness/state-counts/field.md` did not change, and their earlier judgments are carried forward unchanged.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: no move in this range.** The `superRefine` condition is byte-identical (`field.showOnCreate === false && field.required === true`), as are the issue's `code` and `path` and the key's type (`z.boolean().optional()`, no default). Only the comment, the message string, the describe string and the jsdoc changed. Every accept-set judgment of the previous record stands: a pure widening, the refused pair inside the new space, nothing reshaped, no bypass through `fieldPatches`.
- **Public surface.** The describe text of `showOnCreate` changed, and the three reference pages were regenerated to match (one row in `field.mdx`, two each in `object.mdx` and `migration.mdx`). No key, type or export moved. Right.
- **Pin 1, `metadata-protocol` field count 84 to 85.** Right. `main` pins `field: 84`, this PR adds exactly one top-level `FieldSchema` key, and the pin carries its `[#36425]` reason line like its neighbours. The body's note that a second PR adding a field key (#36399) will raise it again is correct and is that PR's to do.
- **Pin 2, `driver-sql` `FIELD_KEY_STORAGE_CLASS.showOnCreate = 'presentation'`.** Right. The file draws the line "at what the DDL reads": no column shape, index or default depends on whether a create surface asks for a field. Its family (`hidden`, `readonly`, `visibleWhen`, `requiredWhen`, and `required` itself under ADR-0113) is all `presentation`, and the row sits beside `hidden`. On a builtin column name the key would still be honoured by the create surfaces, so reporting it as discarded would be false. At runtime an unclassified key is already read as presentation, so the row changes no behaviour.
- **Pin 3, `metadata-core` `FIELD_REFERENCE_POSITIONS.showOnCreate = keep`.** Right. The value is a boolean and names no field, the same reasoning the table gives for `dueLike`, `mailAssociation` and `referenceNameVisible`, and the same class as `hidden` and `readonly` on the line above. A denied field leaves the served `fields` map whole, so the facet of a served field discloses nothing about a denied one. Before the row, the key fell to `unclassified`, which removes a value only when a string or key in it mentions a denied field; a boolean never does. So the served schema is the same before and after, and the row only makes the choice deliberate.
- **Why these three were missed at `197434e9`.** Each is a "classify every `FieldSchema` key" pin in another package. They are not readers of the key, so the previous record's statement that no reader exists still holds, and the ledger grade `planned` still stands.
- **Check-runs on this head.** All concluded, none failed. Green: Test Core and its ten shards, Test UI and its sixteen shards, Build Core, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Type Check UI, Type Check workspace, consumer gates, source gates and debt ledger, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, every Lint run, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Regression Gate. The runs the previous record left as pending are now answered. Skipped runs are the opt-in and schedule ones.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset is still `@objectstack/spec` minor. Right for an `added` key.
- `driver-sql` and `metadata-core` gain source lines and no changeset entry of their own. That is acceptable: both sit in the fixed group with `@objectstack/spec` in `.changeset/config.json`, so they version with it, and neither line changes behaviour. Check Changeset is green.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` still describe the diff. Right.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #36455` on the PR body and the changeset. #36455 is open and carries `domain:skills`. This is better than the earlier `follow-up owed`. Right.
- The changeset's refusal sentence now gives the card's reason and says a `defaultValue` makes no exception because the field is still asked for. It agrees with the message and the describe.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Rulings now on the card.** Comment 7079131071 records the seven seat rulings: the split, the name and absence semantics, the refusal with no `defaultValue` exception and its honest reason (item 3), `requiredWhen` accepted (item 4), action-opened named forms (item 5), the skills card (item 6), and the claim's lines (item 7). The previous record's "rulings cited but not on the card" flag is answered.
- `open_questions` in the os-dev-report is still empty.
- `security_findings: withheld` in the report still has no detail on the card. This round found nothing security-sensitive in the range; the FLS row is judged under ① and holds. The seat's confirmation with the dev is still owed.
- **ADR-0085 §2.** Unchanged. The ADR note is owed on #36086 after the PRs merge, per ruling 2.
- **Card claim.** Still reads `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. Ruling 7 says the seat amends it when PR 2 opens. Not a point against this head.
- **SQL push-down.** The range adds no query, no id materialisation and no join. The one driver file touched gains a row in a classification table. Nothing to flag.
- **Overlap.** GitHub reports the PR mergeable and clean against `main`, which still pins `field: 84`.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts**

S1: closed. The fix took route (b). The ruling is on the card (7079131071 item 3), and the four texts were rewritten: the comment above the refusal, the message, the describe, and the changeset sentence. None of them now says that no create could pass. The reason given is the card's rule, that a required field is always asked for when a record is created so the person creating it sees every value the record must have. The comment says in so many words that the insert would resolve a `defaultValue`, which is what `engine-validate.ts` measures. The engine no longer contradicts the published message.

- The message still names both fixes and the `requiredWhen` alternative. It steers a defaulted field's author to keep the field on create, with its default filled in, which no longer weakens the write contract by implication.
- The jsdoc, the describe and the message agree with one another and with the condition, sentence by sentence.
- Nit: "a required field is always asked for on create" is written as a fact, but it is this key's rule, not the platform's present behaviour. A `required: true` field that is `hidden` or `readonly` is left off the create dialog today (the card's own measurement, 7 of 26 fields), and the schema accepts those pairs. The previous record already named the stricter-than-siblings choice as deliberate. No effect on what parses. Left as an accepted deviation, or tidied when PR 2 touches the describe.
- Carried nit: the describe is in the present tense while no create surface reads the key. The changeset and the ledger say so. No change asked.
- Carried nit: `required: true` with the field's own `visibleWhen` falls under the same ruling.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**packages/spec/src/data/field-show-on-create.test.ts** (implementing)

- The message assertion follows the reworded first sentence (`would leave this field off every create surface`), and the header comment gives the new reason. The five cases and what they pin are otherwise unchanged, so the earlier judgment stands: the refusal is pinned by count, path, code and the object-door path, and the widening by full `safeParse` success on four controls.
- Carried nit: the second case is titled "naming both remedies" and matches only the first sentence, and the `defaultValue` case pins the issue count alone, not the sentence that says a default makes no exception. A test-only tightening, for PR 2 if at all.
- Nit: one line of the header comment runs long after the edit. Lint is green.

**packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/builtin-column-collision.ts** (implementing)

- The row agrees with the file's own contract, as judged under ①. Its comment states the reason. Holds.

**packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts** (implementing)

- The row and its comment agree with the table's contract, as judged under ①. Holds.

**packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts** (implementing)

- The count and its reason line agree with the schema. Holds.

**packages/spec/liveness/field.json** and **packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts** (implementing, unchanged in this range)

- Carried forward: the `planned` row and the `omit` row both agree with the tree. The stand-alone caveat of the previous record also carries: if PR 2 slips past the next release cut, the ledger row should take `authorWarn: true` or the describe a not-yet-enforced marker. A follow-up condition, not a finding on this head.
